title: Battery passport
regulatoryLine: Mapped to Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 Annex XIII and the Battery Pass content guidance, ready ahead of the 18 February 2027 battery passport mandate.

statements.text: Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 is in force; its battery passport obligations apply from 18 February 2027 to the battery categories it covers.
This profile's field-level mapping to Annex XIII, its category applicability and its clause citations are under review against the primary text and the licensed specification.

contextRefs.name: Battery Pass Data Model 1.2.0
contextRefs.licence: CC-BY-4.0, declared in the repository README; no LICENCE file present
contextRefs.use: Vocabulary alignment only. No file from that repository is redistributed here, and its generated JSON Schema is deliberately not used for validation: every property is required by SAMM generation, so no tiered payload can validate.

stamps.description: The sample marker a demonstration record carries first; never product data.
The profile identifier the payload declares.
The profile version the payload declares; a reader decodes under it and never under a newer one.
An optional physical-object DID carried in the public payload; carrying it does not implement physical binding.
The data-carrier identifier (chip UID) the lookup service indexes beside the passport identifier.

fields.label: Passport reference
fields.note: Distinct from the battery identifier: 6.1.2.1(a) expects several passports over one physical battery, because 5.2.1(d) requires a new passport on remanufacture, repurpose or preparation for re-use.

fields.label: Serial number
fields.note: Must comply with ISO/IEC 15459 or equivalent, and should be serialised. The spec deviates from BattReg here deliberately: the regulation attaches the identifier to the model, 6.1.2.2(e) attaches it to the item.

fields.label: Model name
fields.note: Prose by nature: it is whatever the maker calls the model. Length is capped so it fits a label and a passport heading.

fields.label: Responsible operator
fields.note: The operator answering for the passport, which need not be the manufacturer and can change over life.

fields.label: Brand contact
fields.note: 6.1.2.4(c) wants five parts: name, registered trade name or trademark, postal address with a single contact point, web address, e-mail. Our brand record holds one contact string.

fields.label: Place of manufacture
fields.note: Model level, not unit: it is the plant. A record rather than a sentence, so the country is a code a consumer can group and compare on while the plant stays human-readable. `battery@1` put it on the unit and joined it to the date in one free-text string.

fields.label: Made
fields.note: The spec caps this at month; the product owner asked for the day (2026-07-27). Day precision truncates to month, so a reader expecting 6.1.3.2 loses nothing. Item level, unlike the place.

fields.label: Put into service

sourceRefs.name: Date of putting the battery into service

fields.note: Restricted, not public, which is counter-intuitive.

fields.label: Guarantee until
fields.note: Legal warranty period, or the manufacturer guarantee where longer, from the purchase date. Absent from battery@1.

fields.label: Category
fields.note: May change when a new passport is issued, for instance an EV battery repurposed into stationary storage. Consumer wording ("e-bike") stays in the UI; the payload carries the category.

fields.label: Mass
fields.note: The spec says mass, not weight: BattReg says weight, the physically correct quantity is mass (footnote 5, DIN EN ISO 80000-4). Module and cell mass should also be given, for recycling efficiency.

fields.label: Status
fields.note: Our lifecycle already produces this. The spec warns the five words are undefined at source and must travel with a description of the treatments applied.

fields.label: Separate collection symbol
fields.legalBasis: Art. 13(4); Annex VI Part B; Annex XIII (1q)
fields.note: Mandatory on every battery since 18 August 2025. We draw it, nobody types it.

fields.label: Element symbols
fields.note: Required above 0.002% cadmium or 0.004% lead, so derived from the substance figures.

fields.label: Usable extinguishing agent
fields.note: Several agents may be usable, so this takes more than one. Open: the Annex requires the agent to be stated but names no vocabulary, and proprietary agents appear faster than a list is revised.

fields.label: What the symbols mean
fields.note: Standard explanatory copy, the same for every brand. Ours to write once.

fields.label: Declaration of conformity
fields.note: Public document. Needs the attachment seam we do not have yet.

fields.label: Test reports

sourceRefs.name: Results of test reports proving compliance

fields.note: The whole reason the authority tier exists: notified bodies, market surveillance authorities and the Commission, nobody else.

sourceRefs.name: Battery carbon footprint per functional unit
Contribution of raw material acquisition and pre-processing lifecycle stage
Contribution of main product production/manufacturing lifecycle stage
Contribution of end of life and recycling lifecycle stage

fields.label: Carbon class
fields.awaitingAct: Art. 7(2) delegated and implementing acts, not yet adopted
fields.note: The one field that cannot be constrained yet, and the reason is stated rather than worked around: both the class set and the declaration format come from acts under Art. 7(2) that have not been adopted. Offering a guessed A-to-G list would publish our invention as the class scheme. The surface says the format is pending instead of presenting an open box as a free choice. Becomes a closed enum the day the act lands.

fields.label: Footprint study

sourceRefs.name: Web link to public carbon footprint study

fields.note: The declaration alone does not discharge the duty; the study has to be reachable.

fields.label: Battery and brand information
fields.note: The spec points back at 6.1 and 6.2 rather than adding fields.

fields.label: Due diligence report

sourceRefs.name: Information of due diligence report in the battery passport

fields.note: battery@1 takes a reference string. The duty is a published report, so a link is the honest minimum.

fields.label: Third-party assurance
fields.note: A record, because an assurance is only worth what the verifier is worth: naming the scheme without the body that certified against it is unfalsifiable. The scheme name stays open text rather than a list, since recognition itself arrives by implementing and delegated acts under Art. 53.

fields.label: Chemistry
fields.note: An open list, not a closed one: 6.5.2 NOTE records that no unambiguous nomenclature exists yet, so the familiar abbreviations are offered and a value outside them stays valid. The fuller cathode, anode and electrolyte description belongs to electrodeMaterials.

fields.label: Critical raw materials
fields.legalBasis: Annex XIII (1b); Annex VI Part A(10)
fields.note: Those present above 0.1% by weight, selected from Reg. (EU) 2024/1252 Annex II. Closed, because that register is exhaustive by law; it is revised at least every three years, so the mirrored list carries that review duty with it.

fields.label: Cathode, anode and electrolyte materials

sourceRefs.name: Materials used in cathode, anode and electrolyte

fields.note: The spec names three components, so the component is a closed list while the material stays open: chemistry nomenclature is unsettled (6.5.2 NOTE) but which part of a cell you are describing is not. Separator and casing are included because a dismantler needs them and the Annex says "used in", not "used in only these three".

fields.label: Hazardous substances
fields.legalBasis: Annex XIII (1b); Annex VI Part A(8)

constraints.patternHint: Two to seven digits, two digits, then a check digit, as in 7439-92-1

fields.note: Those other than mercury, cadmium and lead. A repeated record rather than a sentence, because each substance needs its own name and CAS number to be machine-checkable. The CAS check digit is computable, so a consumer can verify the number as well as its shape. No closed substance list: the ECHA candidate list runs to hundreds of entries and is revised twice a year, so mirroring it here would go stale between releases.

fields.label: Effects of those substances

sourceRefs.name: Impact of substances on environment, human health, safety, persons

fields.note: Prose by nature, and by duty: Art. 74(1f) requires an explanation of impacts on the environment, human health and safety written for a person to act on. A code list would defeat the purpose of the article.

fields.label: Dismantling manual

sourceRefs.name: Dismantling information: manuals for the removal and the disassembly of the battery pack

fields.note: The duty is the manual, not a reference to one. battery@1 stores a document number.

fields.label: Spare parts: postal address

sourceRefs.name: Postal address of sources of spare parts

fields.note: A record rather than one box, so the country is a code and the rest stays as postal services expect. Postcode is optional because several countries have none.

fields.label: Spare parts: e-mail

sourceRefs.name: E-mail address of sources of spare parts

fields.note: Deliberately a permissive shape check, not RFC 5322: the aim is to catch a typo before publication, and a pattern strict enough to be correct rejects addresses that work. 254 is the practical maximum length.

sourceRefs.name: Web address of sources of spare parts

fields.label: Safety measures
fields.note: Restricted and detailed. Distinct from the public consumer safety line battery@1 carries as `safety`.

fields.label: Recycled content

sourceRefs.name: Pre-consumer and post-consumer recycled cobalt, lithium, nickel and lead share

fields.note: The umbrella figure over the eight splits below. Scoped per model per year per manufacturing plant, which is finer than model level alone. Annex C carries the mandatory targets.

fields.label: Making it last

sourceRefs.name: Information on the role of end-users in contributing to waste prevention

fields.note: Information, not a document. The clause asks what the end user should do; a sentence on the passport answers that where a linked PDF defers it. Typed as a document until 2026-07-28, which is why the consumer page carried three labels with nothing behind them: the attachment seam is G16, so a document can only be a link, and a sample can only ever declare a reserved host. A brand holding a real document declares its URL here and the surface links it, because the care block sorts on the value rather than the type.

fields.label: Where to return it

sourceRefs.name: Information on the role of end-users in contributing to the separate collection of waste batteries

fields.note: battery@1 carried this as a sentence, which reads better on a consumer page than a linked PDF. Retyped from document to text on 2026-07-28 to do what that note asked for, matching the textile registry, which answers the same question in prose and reads the better for it.

fields.label: End of life

sourceRefs.name: Information on battery collection, preparation for second life and on treatment at end of life

fields.note: Retyped with the other two end-user clauses on 2026-07-28. What actually happens to the battery is a thing a reader can be told in three sentences, and a document reference tells them nothing at all until they open it.

fields.label: Rated capacity
fields.legalBasis: Annex IV Part A(1); Annex VI Part A(6)
fields.note: Ampere-hours. battery@1 held a free string and the sample filled it with 630 Wh, which is energy: a different attribute (6.7.2.5).

fields.label: Capacity fade
fields.note: Model level and static in the spec: the declared fade characteristic, not this unit’s measured loss.

fields.label: Usable energy
fields.legalBasis: added by the consortium, based on UN GTR No 22

fields.label: Remaining usable energy
fields.legalBasis: added by the consortium, based on UN GTR No 22

fields.label: Remaining power
fields.legalBasis: Annex VII Part A(2); Annex IV

sourceRefs.name: Ratio between nominal battery power and battery energy

fields.label: Round trip efficiency at half life

sourceRefs.name: Round trip energy efficiency at 50% of cycle-life

fields.label: Internal resistance, pack

sourceRefs.name: Initial internal resistance of battery pack

fields.note: Decimal, not an integer: an internal resistance is tens of milliohms, so whole ohms would round every honest value to nought. The unit stays as the spec declares it and the type stops discarding the quantity.

fields.label: Internal resistance, cell

sourceRefs.name: Initial internal resistance of battery cell

fields.note: Decimal, not an integer: an internal resistance is tens of milliohms, so whole ohms would round every honest value to nought. The unit stays as the spec declares it and the type stops discarding the quantity.

fields.label: Internal resistance, module

sourceRefs.name: Initial internal resistance of battery module

fields.note: Decimal, not an integer: an internal resistance is tens of milliohms, so whole ohms would round every honest value to nought. The unit stays as the spec declares it and the type stops discarding the quantity.

sourceRefs.name: Internal resistance increase of battery pack
Internal resistance increase of battery cell
Internal resistance increase of battery module

fields.label: Expected life in years
fields.note: Restricted, while the cycle count below is public.

sourceRefs.name: Expected lifetime: number of charge-discharge cycles
Number of full charging and discharging cycles

fields.label: Cycle life test used
fields.note: Without the test, the cycle figure is not comparable between brands. Open: the applicable standard differs by category and JTC 24 and IEC are still issuing them.

sourceRefs.name: Temperature range idle state, lower boundary
Temperature range idle state, upper boundary
Time spent in extreme temperatures above boundary
Time spent in extreme temperatures below boundary
Time spent charging during extreme temperatures above boundary
Time spent charging during extreme temperatures below boundary

fields.label: Safety
fields.legalBasis: app addition; the spec puts safety measures at 6.6.1.5, restricted

sourceRefs.name: not in the spec: plain-language safety line

fields.note: Prose by nature: a plain-language line a consumer reads on the passport. The spec's own safety measures at 6.6.1.5 sit in the restricted tier, so this is the public summary of them, not a substitute.

fields.label: State of health
fields.legalBasis: app addition; the spec decomposes SoH into Annex VII Part A parameters

sourceRefs.name: not in the spec: state of health as a single figure

fields.note: Annex VII has no single SoH figure: it lists remaining capacity, remaining power, remaining round trip efficiency, self-discharge evolution and resistance. Our one number is a summary, and should be presented as one.

fields.label: Measured by

sourceRefs.name: not in the spec: who measured, and when

fields.note: Closed, and closable because the attribute is ours rather than the spec's: no consumer outside the app depends on this vocabulary, so fixing it costs no interop. Who measured decides how much a reading is worth.

eventMappings.requires: manufacturing or commissioning evidence naming the facility, time and responsible party; the native ACTIVATE alone records only that a passport was opened

eventMappings.externalEvent: physical move or change of custody
eventMappings.requires: actual source and destination movement or custody evidence; a change of token control is not a shipment

eventMappings.externalEvent: physical move or change of custody
eventMappings.requires: actual source and destination movement or custody evidence
custody evidence beyond the token transfer; the transfer of token control alone establishes neither physical movement nor legal title
repair evidence naming what was done, by whom and when
nothing physical: an EDIT is a native metadata operation and maps to a record revision, not a physical transformation

eventMappings.externalEvent: disposition, or a process creating new products or materials
eventMappings.requires: recycling evidence distinguishing disposition of this item from a process whose outputs carry new identities

sourceRefs.use: The legal instrument behind the critical raw materials list.

sourceRefs.name: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, for every value typed country
Critical Raw Materials Act, Annex II Section 1
sourceRefs.use: The closed option list for criticalRawMaterials. Revised at least every three years, so a consumer should check the list date rather than assume permanence.

sourceRefs.name: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2
sourceRefs.use: Every value typed country. Officially assigned codes only; user-assigned and exceptionally-reserved codes are excluded so a passport cannot name a place no register resolves.

sourceRefs.name: CAS Registry Number
sourceRefs.use: The pattern on hazardousSubstances.cas. The final digit is a check digit, so a consumer can verify the number arithmetically and not only its shape.

identity.passportIdentifier: A GS1 Digital Link URI carrying the GTIN under application identifier 01 and the serial under 21 (spec/record-model.md section 3); the enduring identifier never changes across the chain.
